summary: Dedicated: noisy-neighbor-like p95/p99 spikes when long-context summarization runs alongside interactive chat traffic
description:
Customer reports intermittent tail spikes that look like noisy-neighbor contention on their Dedicated cluster.

Issue summary
- NorthPeak Analytics (Dedicated) sees p95 and p99 latency spikes on interactive chat route during windows when long-context summarization jobs run.
- Customer expectation: Dedicated = isolated capacity; they suspect another tenant. Initial check indicates isolation is correct; contention is within their own workload mix (short interactive + long prefill-heavy requests) sharing the same GPU pool.

Impact
- Chat endpoint intermittently breaches customer’s internal SLO during summarization runs.
- Symptoms: request queue buildup + elevated time-to-first-token (TTFT) on short prompts; total latency increases primarily driven by wait time.

Environment
- Dedicated cluster: npk-ded-us-east-03
- Region: us-east
- Models: llama-3.1-70b-instruct
- Routes (customer terminology):
  - /chat (interactive, streaming)
  - /summarize (batchy, long context, non-streaming)

Customer-provided time window
- 2024-11-12 19:05–20:10 UTC (repeatable when their summarization pipeline starts)

Steps to reproduce (Redwood)
1) Reproduce mixed workload on same Dedicated pool with a long-context prefill-heavy workload at moderate QPS.
2) Add short streaming chat traffic (low token count) and observe TTFT/p95.
3) Compare baseline FIFO scheduler vs prototype short/long prompt-aware scheduler (feature-flagged).

Observations / investigation notes (internal)
- Verified no cross-tenant mixing: Dedicated pool and node assignment are correct.
- Queueing metrics indicate short requests are occasionally blocked behind long prefill batches (priority inversion pattern).
- Tail driven by:
  - elevated scheduler wait time (queue wait), not decode speed
  - batching behavior pulling long prefill work ahead of short requests
- Hypothesis: mixed workload contention in runtime scheduler; FIFO + batching allows long prefill to inflate tail latency for short requests.

Artifacts / breadcrumbs
- Slack: #incidents thread on queue depth growth during canary build (reference only; not customer-visible): sources/slack/incidents/thread_1731462200_900114.json
- Similar pattern seen in SUP-2194 (p95 spikes during long-prompt batch windows) and SUP-2201 (timeouts under burst traffic).

Ask from customer
- Confirm whether this is expected behavior and what isolation guarantees apply within a single Dedicated pool.
- Provide mitigations and a plan to improve tail under mixed workloads.

Proposed path
- Short term: mitigate by workload separation or admission controls.
- Medium term: offer opt-in runtime scheduler prototype (mixed-workload scheduler feature flag) to reduce tail latency impact.

Workaround options discussed
1) Separate pools (preferred): move /summarize to a separate Dedicated pool or separate route-to-pool mapping to eliminate intra-tenant contention.
2) Admission control by class: cap concurrency for long-context/summarization to protect interactive queue (backpressure).
3) Enable scheduler prototype flag in a canary slice after we validate on their workload trace.

Resolution (current)
- Confirmed root cause is within-tenant mixed workload contention (not cross-tenant).
- Customer agreed to temporary mitigation: cap summarization concurrency during peak chat hours + schedule summarization off-peak.
- Redwood to run a trace-based replay (customer-provided distribution) in our mixed workload suite and propose an opt-in canary with the new scheduler flag.

Follow-ups
- Provide customer a short write-up explaining Dedicated isolation (tenant isolation) vs intra-tenant route contention and recommended architecture.
- Internal: link this case to mixed-workload scheduler canary execution and ensure guardrails/alerts cover starvation and backlog growth.
